high.title: Yen Clings to Intervention Gains as Traders Stay Alert to More
high.summary: The yen sustained gains following coordinated intervention by Tokyo and Washington authorities, putting broad pressure on the US dollar. The Fed's decision to hold interest rates steady further weakened dollar sentiment, with investors unwinding long-dollar positions. Speculative traders remain cautious about rebuilding bearish yen positions, suggesting the intervention effect may persist near-term. Falling oil prices added to dollar headwinds globally.

medium.title: Ahead of Market: 10 Things That Will Decide Stock Market Action on Tuesday
medium.summary: Indian equities staged a strong rally, with the Sensex gaining 544 points and the Nifty surging approximately 1.6%, adding nearly ₹5 lakh crore (~$60bn) in market capitalisation in a single session. The primary catalyst was easing crude oil prices following renewed US-Iran diplomatic talks, which provided meaningful relief to India's import-heavy economy and the INR. A stronger rupee and continued FII inflows further reinforced positive sentiment, alongside upbeat corporate earnings. For INR and bond traders, the combination of softer oil and FII buying is constructive — lower crude reduces India's current account deficit pressure, a key structural driver of INR weakness. Sustained FII inflows also support the rupee via increased USD supply in the spot market. Watch whether oil prices hold at lower levels and whether FII momentum continues into Tuesday's session, as a reversal in either could quickly dampen the risk-on tone.

medium.title: These 7 Banking Stocks Have an Upside Potential of Up to 25% in 1 Year, According to Analysts
medium.summary: Analysts are flagging select banking stocks as compelling plays on the back of what appears to be a structural shift in FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investor) behaviour, with last month's inflows cited as potentially the beginning of a sustained trend rather than a one-off event. Banking stocks are highlighted as the most direct proxy for India's economic growth trajectory, making them a natural destination for incremental foreign capital. For macro and FX-focused investors, sustained FPI buying into Indian banking equities is directly relevant — it represents USD-to-INR conversion flows that support rupee stability and can compress USD/INR. Additionally, a re-rating of banking stocks tends to signal broader confidence in India's credit cycle and RBI's policy stance. Monitor whether FPI flows into financials broaden and deepen, and watch for any RBI commentary on systemic liquidity that could influence bank earnings expectations.

medium.title: Oil Price Today (August 4): Crude Oil Nears $85 as Peace Talks Uncertainty Looms After Fresh Attacks
medium.summary: Crude oil prices edged higher toward $85/barrel following renewed Middle East supply concerns, as diplomatic progress stalled amid fresh reported attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping chokepoint. Monday's sharp losses were partially reversed, though analysts expect prices to cool as non-conflict zone supply expands. For India — the world's third-largest crude importer — sustained oil prices near $85 represent a meaningful macro risk: every $10/barrel increase in crude widens India's current account deficit by approximately 0.4% of GDP and exerts direct downward pressure on the INR. Elevated crude also complicates the RBI's inflation management task and could delay any potential rate easing cycle. Fund managers should monitor Hormuz shipping disruption data and OPEC+ response signals closely.

medium.title: Copper Hits Two-Month High Above $14,000 as Inventories Dip
medium.summary: Copper surged above $14,000 to a two-month high, driven by tightening LME warehouse inventories — now at just over one day's global consumption — and optimism around a potential Iran conflict resolution. Aluminium also rallied to its highest since June 23, with broad-based gains across base metals. While copper is not a direct INR driver, a broad commodity rally signals improving global risk appetite and potential demand recovery, which is broadly supportive of emerging market capital inflows including India. Rising metal prices also benefit Indian metal sector equities (Nifty Metal index), which could provide incremental support to the broader Sensex/Nifty. Watch whether this rally sustains as a leading indicator of global industrial demand recovery.
